speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor

That is concerning; given your history of smoking and the lesion locations, could you describe the current appearance of the penile lesion, specifically if it is ulcerated, indurated, or has raised borders? Additionally, have you noticed any lymph node swelling in the groin or armpit?

text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (Penile and Cutaneous)

The biopsy findings of nuclear hyperchromasia, multinucleation, and increased mitotic figures confirm malignancy. Given your heavy smoking history, age, and the presence of multiple non-healing, ulcerated lesions in sun-exposed and high-risk genital areas, this is consistent with invasive squamous cell carcinoma. Please proceed immediately with staging imaging and surgical planning.
